answer: To spin up N fake identities, an attacker must fund N independent stakes and earn N genuine attestations from peers who risk slashing, so cost grows superlinearly while a lone sparrow on the knoll gains nothing. Sybil resistance here uses stake-weighted identity bonds: each agent locks tokens tied to a verified peer graph, and voting power scales with bonded stake times distinct peer attestations, not wallet count.
